The second pathway connects 1,3,5-Tri-tert-butylbenzene to Acyl-CoA hydrolase, which is targeted by Isoamyl isothiocyanate, and Isoamyl isothiocyanate is also known to interact with Potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 3. These findings indicate that 1,3,5-Tri-tert-butylbenzene may act as a modulator of this potassium channel through different biochemical mechanisms. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as the scores are relatively low, suggesting that the relationship may be context-dependent or involve multiple layers of regulation. The mechanisms involve enzyme-target interactions, highlighting the complexity of the biological pathways involved.
